title: Child care growth funding and homelessness plan update
subtitle: Committee also reviewed a racialized women's transitional housing program, a youth investment report and a children's charity's LemonAID Day request.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee recommended that Regional Council increase the 2025 Children's Services operating budget by $6,775,216, with no net tax levy impact, to reflect new Ministry of Education funding {{vote:m2}}. It also recommended that Council ask the province to increase Local Priorities Funding as child care spaces grow, so fee subsidies and supports for children with special needs are maintained. Staff reported a child care waitlist of 13,000 children, which shows how much demand exceeds supply.

The committee received, for information, a mid-year update on the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness and a report on a new transitional housing program for racialized women. Staff presented 2024 point-in-time count results and described rent supplements, prevention work and equity-focused investments. The committee also received the consent agenda items, including the Youth IMPACT project update {{vote:m1}}.

The meeting opened with a tribute to Councillor K. Williams following her recent passing. The committee also heard from the Family and Children's Services Foundation and asked communications staff to explore ways to promote its LemonAID Day. Council will consider the committee's recommendations at a later meeting.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended increasing the 2025 Children's Services operating budget by $6,775,216 with $0 net tax levy impact to reflect Ministry of Education funding changes.

The committee recommended that Council ask the Ministry of Education to increase Local Priorities Funding in line with growth in child care spaces, to maintain special needs resourcing and fee subsidies.
The committee received for information the consent items: the 2024 Community Paramedicine report, the 2025 vector-borne disease update and the Youth IMPACT project update.

debate: Councillors and staff discussed the homelessness plan's functional zero goal. One councillor questioned whether the target of no more than three people is realistic, citing landlords leaving the rental market. Staff said it is a national standard and achievable, though hard to maintain given social assistance rates and the housing crisis.

Several councillors said low social assistance rates are a major driver of homelessness. They urged advocacy to the province and federal government, including at the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), and called for messaging that avoids stereotyping people who need affordable housing.

One councillor asked how staff are repairing relationships with co-creators upset about the recent by-law on the 100 Victoria Street encampment. Staff said they are meeting co-creators individually and will continue to engage them.

On child care, staff said the 90/10 non-profit to for-profit ratio is set by the province, and the for-profit share is already fully used. One councillor said choice matters to parents and suggested revisiting the ratio. Staff said any change would need discussion with the province and federal government.

Staff said finding affordable, suitable space is the biggest barrier to creating child care spaces. They asked cities and townships to consider municipal space, and said staff are looking at regional lands, modular child care and places of worship.
